subject: Private vs Dedicated for HelixBio genomics pilot — GPU slate proposal
messages:
From: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@helixbio.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixbio.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixBio pilot - isolation requirements + sizing ask

Hi Irene —

Thanks for taking this on. As discussed in the demo, HelixBio is ready to run a 3-month pilot analyzing de-identified genomic fragments. Two quick constraints for you and the team:

- Compliance: we need an environment that meets our legal counsel's isolation requirements (data residency in us-west, audit logs, and KMS integration).
- Throughput: target is ~75–120 concurrent requests at peak, average payload ~1.5k tokens, target P99 latency < 600ms for inference-only calls.

We need a recommendation on whether we should run the pilot on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) or Redwood Private (VPC/private deployment). Please include a concrete GPU slate (instance types / GPU counts), expected throughput/latency per config, lead time for provisioning, and any procurement/PO implications.

Can you also attach a lightweight sizing spreadsheet so our infra and procurement teams can review?

Appreciate it — Sam
Sam Brooks
Director, ML Ops
HelixBio
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Brooks <sam.brooks@helixbio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixBio pilot - isolation requirements + sizing ask

Sam — thanks, this is clear and a good pilot scope. High level recommendation up front: run the 3-month pilot on Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity sized for steady-state peak, and enable a Private (VPC-hosted) fallback for the first two weeks of sensitive ingest/validation. That gives you predictable latency/cost while we satisfy audit and KMS integration requirements.

Attached is a quick sizing spreadsheet (helix_pilot_sizing_v1.xlsx) with two vetted configurations:

Option A — Dedicated (fastest time-to-live):
- GPU slate: 4 x A100 80GB (or 2 x H100 80GB depending on availability)
- Expected steady throughput: ~90 concurrent requests (with batching)
- P99 inference: ~450–550ms (model: opt-1.3b-like baseline, int8 quantized path)
- Lead time: provisioning on hosted Dedicated: ~5–7 business days; no on-prem setup.
- Pros: rapid onboarding, lower procurement friction, easy burst scaling.

Option B — Private VPC (isolation-first):
- GPU slate: 2 x H100 80GB nodes (on customer VPC or dedicated colo) + 1 failover node
- Expected steady throughput: ~60–80 concurrent requests
- P99 inference: ~400–600ms depending on network egress overhead and model variant
- Lead time: ~3–5 weeks (network + KMS + audit configurations)
- Pros: strongest isolation and audit footprint; cons are longer lead time and higher ops coordination.

Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- Hybrid approach: start Dedicated for week 0–2, route sensitive uploads to Private VPC for validation, then cut over. This shortens time-to-value while preserving your compliance gating.
- Autoscaling: we recommend a steady baseline on reserved GPUs and burst pool enabled for unpredictable spikes; this minimizes cost while meeting P99 SLOs.
- Model hygiene: enable KV prefix caching for repeated fragments and a short-lived response cache to shave 10–15% off token costs.

I attached the sizing workbook. Happy to pair with procurement on PO language if needed. Calling out next steps below.

Next steps:
1) Review & confirm preferred option (A/B/hybrid) — Helix infra + procurement.
2) If Dedicated, sign the 3-month reserved commitment (we'll share SOW/pricing).
3) If Private, schedule pre-onboarding network checklist call with our infra team.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam — looping in pricing and procurement details. High level pricing options for the 3-month pilot (ballpark, final pricing on request):

- Dedicated pilot (Option A): 3-month reserved commitment for 4 x A100 80GB equivalent — $68k/month (committed rate), includes standard SLA and 5-day provisioning SLA.
- Private VPC (Option B): one-time onboarding engineering fee $18k + monthly infra ops of $95k/month (includes 24/7 monitoring, audit log retention 12 months).

If you want a hybrid (start Dedicated then migrate to Private), we can offer a 20% credit toward the Private onboarding fee if the Dedicated commitment converts within 90 days.

Procurement notes: please reference our HubSpot deal HS-54877 when issuing PO; if procurement requires a SOW or contract redlines, let us know and we can prioritize legal review.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixBio pilot - isolation requirements + sizing ask

Sam / team — technical addendum with concrete GPU tiling and perf expectations: 

- Model profile: we validated with a 1.3B encoder-decoder tuned to your preprocessing. With int8 quantization and kernel fusion we get ~1.8–2.2 token/s per A100 80GB per stream; batching increases aggregate throughput.
- Suggested shard/tiling for Option A (Dedicated): 4 x A100s configured as 2 shards (2 GPUs per shard) to maximize KV cache locality. This layout reduces cross-GPU NVLink traffic and keeps P99 consistent under load.
- Suggested layout for Option B (Private): 2 x H100 nodes where each node runs 2 inference workers pinned to separate GPUs; network egress will be the main variance so enable an internal NLB and private peering.
- Autoscale policy (recommended): baseline at 70% concurrency with burst to +50% capacity on a warm standby; scale decisions controlled by queue depth and 95th token latency.
- Cost estimate: inference unit cost ~ $0.62–0.85 per 1k tokens on Dedicated A100 path (after batching and caching). Private path is ~20–30% higher due to ops and fixed onboarding amortization.

I attached a short runbook in the sizing sheet for canary traffic routing and traffic-splitting rules. Happy to run a 2-hour remote sizing workshop with Helix infra next week — suggest Mon/Tue preferred.

— Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform
